hints.title: Replace each mean by its total
hints.body: Let the two sets contain n and m data values. Before the exchange their totals are 15n and 20m. An exchange changes the values in each set but not the number of values in either set.
hints.recap: The total of a data set equals its mean multiplied by its number of values.
hints.pitfall: The two means cannot be averaged equally unless the set sizes are equal.
hints.pause: Write the new total of each set using its new mean.

recall.reminder: The total of a data set equals its mean multiplied by its number of values.

hints.title: Use the unchanged combined total
hints.body: After the exchange the totals are 16n and 17m. Nothing was added to or removed from the combined data, so 15n+20m=16n+17m.
hints.recap: Moving values between groups conserves the overall total.
hints.pitfall: The separate totals change, so it is their sum that stays fixed, not either individual total.
hints.pause: Simplify the equation to find the ratio of the two set sizes.

recall.reminder: Moving values between groups conserves the overall total.

hints.title: Use the counts as weights
hints.body: Simplify the conservation equation to obtain the ratio of the group sizes. Then divide their combined total by their combined number of observations.
hints.recap: A pooled mean uses observation counts as weights.
hints.pitfall: The actual group sizes are unnecessary if their ratio is known.
hints.pause: Derive the count ratio and use it to calculate the pooled mean.

recall.reminder: A pooled mean uses observation counts as weights.

solution:
1. Name the unknown counts. Let the two sets contain n and m values. Their initial totals are 15n and 20m, and their totals after the exchange are 16n and 17m.

2. Conserve the combined total. 15n+20m=16n+17m, so n=3m.

3. Divide total by count. The combined mean is 15n+20mn+m=45m+20m3m+m=654=1614.

Answer A. The larger set has three times the weight of the smaller set.
knowledgePattern: Infer sample-size ratio from conservation of total after a swap
